lines.trans: Director, you are finished.
What are you talking about? I am just getting started.
Still, there is one way to save yourself. Please kill me.
Make it look as though I died of AIDS.
There is a new religious group down south. Please buy it.

words.reading: シンコウシュウキョウ

lines.trans: In the meantime, I will seclude myself in the mountains and be resurrected.
Let us launch a religion with you as the founder and me as the shrine maiden.
Are you telling me to become a cult founder?
As the economy collapses, people will seek healing. With this business, we can surely make a comeback.
Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Noun derived from 終わる (to end).

examples.text: これで今日の授業は終わりです。
examples.trans: With this, today's class is over.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Native Japanese counter for general objects and abstract things like reasons.

examples.text: 理由がもう一つあります。
りんごを一つください。

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: be saved; be rescued; be a big help
meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb; 助かったよ means 'you saved me / that was a huge help'.

examples.text: 俺はトシだ。助かったよ。
手伝ってもらえて助かりました。
お前らが池沢とのケンカに勝てる方法が一つある。
examples.trans: There is one way you guys can win your fight against Ikezawa.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。
エイズで死んだことにして。
examples.trans: Make it look as though I died of AIDS.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Godan verb; past tense is 死んだ.

examples.text: 金魚が死んでしまった。

examples.trans: I don't want to die yet.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: 九州に新興宗教が一つあります。それを買ってください。
examples.trans: There is a new religious group down south. Please buy it.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

meanings.en: cause; bring about; wake someone up
meanings.note: Godan transitive verb; 騒ぎを起こす means 'cause a commotion'.

examples.text: 次に騒ぎを起こしたら追い出すぞ。
examples.trans: If you cause a commotion next time, I'll throw you out.

examples.text: 朝七時に起こしてください。
examples.trans: Please wake me up at 7 a.m.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

examples.text: わたくしたちは二人で一つの生き物なんです。一人で歩いてみて分かりました。

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.
